Breakfast.

At the scheduled time, transfer to the international airport for your flight home.

On the way to the airport, you can extend your visit with a stop at the Larco Museum (Museo Larco), one of Peru’s best-known museums. Its collections showcase the rich legacy of the country’s ancient civilizations.

Founded in 1926 by archaeologist Rafael Larco Hoyle, the museum occupies an 18th-century colonial mansion built on the site of an ancient pre-Columbian structure.

The collection contains around 45,000 objects from civilizations that lived in what is now Peru long before the rise of the Inca. Ceramics, antique textiles, gold and silver jewelry, ritual objects, and archaeological finds trace the development of these societies over thousands of years.

A highlight is the museum’s collection of Moche ceramics, including pieces with erotic imagery that reflect ancient Peruvian ideas about life, fertility, and belief.

A visit to the museum offers a closer look at Peru’s cultural heritage before you head home.

Optional excursion: USD 65 per person.

The trip starts in Lima and passes through Cusco, the ancient Inca capital, and Machu Picchu before climbing to Lake Titicaca. A catamaran takes you to the Island of the Sun. After traveling to La Paz, you’ll visit the Valley of the Moon and Tiwanaku before returning to Lima.
